summary: Round 2: the round-1 major is resolved. The engine now gives tubes their mass (density x section x length, 4.3 g each) and the XT60 has a sourced 3.5 g. The 765 g all-up mass is checked against a 790 g budget derived from twr (1625 g / 2.0 = 812 g, less ~20 g of unmodelled hardware), and twr is 2.12 / twr_sag 1.90. ring_low now has 1732 mm² of web and boss contact on the bed, and every horizontal hole has a teardrop. All FEA cases pass at SF 3 at the 790 g budget, with peaks at load or fixture patches, not at geometric roots. Only minor items remain: the documentation is stale on which ring_low features touch the bed, the remaining s5 fillets and chamfers, and a tight leg deflection margin.

findings.issue: Remaining s5 detail. ENGINEERING.md s5 says inside corners on any load path get r >= 1 mm and outside edges a 0.5-1 mm chamfer. It is a rule, not a margin-dependent option. The motor_hub fork, arm and lug roots carry all of the thrust, and the gimbal_outer pad-to-ring corners carry it too; neither has a fillet, and no part has bed-edge chamfers. The static FEA margins (>= 3.6x on top of SF 3; the hub and ring peaks sit at the dowel bore and servo pad, not the roots) make this low risk. That is why it stays minor, but it does not waive the rule on a part that sees motor vibration.
findings.fix: Add 1-1.5 mm fillets at the hub fork, arm and lug-to-disc vertical inside edges and at the gimbal_outer pad-to-ring inside corners (features.safe_fillet, same pattern as the ring_low disc corners), plus 0.5 mm bed-edge chamfers. Re-run gimbal_fea and outer_fea.

findings.issue: The Parts table (DESIGN.md:95) still says 'bosses, webs and ribs on the bed'. The STL shows the webs and bosses at z 0 (1732 mm²) and the lug ribs 8 mm up on supports, as the ring_low docstring now says correctly.
findings.fix: Change the row to 'bosses and webs (18 mm) on the bed; plate and 10 mm lug ribs on supports'.

findings.issue: leg_fea deflection is 2.948 mm against its 3.0 mm limit (98 %) at the 790 g budget. Stress is fine (3.34 vs 16 MPa). If the build gains mass or the foot load case grows, this is the first check to fail.
findings.fix: Either accept it as is (it is elastic, at a 3 g two-leg landing), or deepen the strut slightly (e.g. a top profile of 20 instead of 18 mm) for headroom.

findings.issue: Both peaks are at load or fixture patches, not geometry. lug_fea peaks at 10.97 MPa at [-42.6, 27.1, 75.4], which is the inner insert site of leg_2 (r 50, 150 deg) on the lug underside. leg_fea peaks at [8.9, 5.5, -4.3], the edge of the pad bearing box. Both are fine, but the coarse 5785-element ring_low mesh means the insert-site stress is only indicative.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally refine the mesh locally at the insert sites.
